output.summary: The problem is not slow customer replies, as SH-CS asked. Customers are charged twice because idempotency-key enforcement was switched off on the gateway (CHG-77, 2026-09-09), so timeout retries went out without a key and were captured again (E-01, E-02, E-03). The release is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION: it only detects and monitors duplicate captures, retry keys and ticket volume. It does not re-enable enforcement.
key_points: Duplicate captures began on 2026-09-09: 118 on 09-09 and 124 on 09-10, versus 0 on 09-07 and 09-08 (E-01).
Config audit shows CHG-77 turned enforcement from on to off on 09-09, noted as temporary, with no rollback executed (E-02).
PSP logs show all 242 duplicate orders on 09-09..10 came from keyless timeout retries. In 09-01..08 all 238 retries carried keys and were deduplicated (E-03).
Double-charge tickets rose from 9 and 11 per week to 288 and 301 with flat order volume. The complaints are a symptom of a new fault (E-05).
The apology-assistant hypothesis (H-COMMUNICATION-GAP) was rejected, as were the retry-bug, PSP-side and perceived-duplicate hypotheses. H-IDEMPOTENCY-DISABLED was confirmed.
Released scope: verify_duplicate_capture_rate on payments-db, verify_retry_keys on psp-logs, and monitor_ticket_volume on crm-tickets. At least 4 orders still have 2 captures and no refund (E-07).

The proposed fix is to re-enable enforcement through set_capture_idempotency. It needs SH-OPS runtime confirmation, and the change is reversible (E-06). It is blocked by VOB-U-AFFECTED-CUSTOMERS, so it is outside the release.
The decision has no holds. The DEFINE gate was CONDITIONAL_PASS, and the open item is tracked as a verification obligation outside the release scope.
limitations_explained: The fix is not applied. Re-enabling enforcement is blocked by the open VOB-U-AFFECTED-CUSTOMERS, so duplicates may continue until SH-OPS confirms and runs it.
The number of double-charged customers and how many were refunded is unknown (U-AFFECTED-CUSTOMERS). E-07 lists only 4 unrefunded orders and does not give totals.
Customers already double-charged are not fixed by the rollback. Refunds (SR-REFUND-AFFECTED-CUSTOMERS) are a separate process owned by SH-OPS.
Whether re-enabling brings back the capture latency SH-PAY was debugging is unknown (U-LATENCY-CAUSE). Assumption A-REENABLE-NO-LATENCY is not supported by the evidence.
The assumption that retries continue at about 120 per day rests partly on the SH-PAY statement (A-RETRY-RATE-STEADY, E-04), which is not authoritative.
